items.title: Meta sued in Australian class action over alleged social media harm to children
items.description: A class-action lawsuit has been filed in an Australian ​court against Meta Platforms’ Facebook and Instagram ‌that alleges the social media platforms exposed children to harmful content and kept them addicted through algorithms. The lawsuit, filed in ​the Federal Court, Australia’s second-highest, by law ​firm MinterEllison this month could be the first ⁠in Australia to blame social media for harming ​its users, particularly children and teenagers. The class-action suit has been filed on behalf of eight plaintiffs who allege Meta harmed them while they were under ​18 and are seeking compensation. “We are aware of ​this claim and we will defend ourselves vigorously,” a Meta ‌spokesperson ⁠said by email. In a suppression order on Monday, the court prohibited reporting any information that could reveal the applicants’ identities and the statement of claim. The ​lawsuit comes ⁠amid rising tensions between Australia and Big Tech after a world-first ban on social ​media for children under 16, and newly ​proposed ⁠rules that could let users switch off algorithm-driven content on their feeds. Meta in August agreed to pay $18 billion to settle ⁠with ​nearly all US states to ​resolve claims it designed social media to addict children.

items.title: ‘Letting roots of Pak-India conflict fester invites more danger’
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Failure to address the underlying disputes that engender crises between Pakistan and India could lead to more dangerous confrontations in the future, a former chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee warned on Wednesday. “Terminating a crisis without addressing its root causes only sets the stage for the next, more dangerous conflict,” retired Gen Zubair Mahmood Hayat said at the concluding session of the second Islamabad Non-Proliferation Conference, organised by the Strategic Vision Institute (SVI). Ex-CJCSC warns against ignoring Kashmir dispute, Indus treaty suspension He said that in the subcontinent, the core issue of Jammu and Kashmir could not be wished away or reduced to an administrative matter. “Similarly, water cannot be converted from a shared necessity into an instrument of power and pressure,” he said while stressing the need for resolution of the Kashmir dispute and restoration of the Indus Waters Treaty. Gen Hayat warned that repeated crises between the nuclear-armed neighbours could become increasingly dangerous if unresolved disputes, diminishing restraint and the absence of sustained political dialogue continued to undermine regional security. Referring to the May 2025 conflict , he said Pakistan had demonstrated its military capabilities and political control through a calibrated response that denied India a unilateral fait accompli without pursuing an unlimited war. “The larger lesson is not that conflict between two nuclear-armed neighbours can be made routine; it is that there is no tested and certified safe space for war,” he said, warning that future crises would involve different leaders, emerging technologies and shorter decision-making timelines, heightening the risk of miscalculation. He said South Asia lacked an inclusive regional security framework, effective crisis-management mechanisms and sustained political dialogue. “The region lives between deterrence that prevents the worst and disputes that repeatedly regenerate danger,” he said. Gen Hayat warned unverified allegations could trigger conflict before the facts were established, with a future confrontation potentially arising from an accident rather than a deliberate state decision. He cited the continuing Operation Sindoor in this context. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

items.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to resume peace talks next month

The Kremlin said the new three-way peace talks, which would be at a technical level, could take ​place in Abu Dhabi and would be focused on how to guarantee the security of Ukraine and Russia once the war ended. They could begin sometime on or ⁠after November 10, it said. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who supports the US proposal for three-way talks with Russia and the United States at the negotiator level, said the talks are to be held as soon as possible, preferably no later than early November. As diplomatic efforts are ongoing, strikes on the front line have not yet come to a halt. Kyiv, capital of Ukraine, was struck by Russian ​ballistic missiles on ​Wednesday evening, which damaged infrastructure and public facilities while injuring six people, according to Vitali Klitschko, mayor of Kyiv. Meanwhile, European leaders will seek to agree on how to finance Ukraine's €70 billion (about $78.6 billion) unmet needs in 2027 at ​a special summit on November 26 and 27, where ‌they will also discuss the EU's next long-term budget, an official from the bloc involved in preparations said. items.title: Saudis intercept more drones as conflict with Houthis spirals
items.description: • Coalition downs six drones launched towards cities, including Madina, as interception debris kills two • Rebels deny ‘deep operations’ in Saudi territory • Iran says Egypt entering Yemen war makes situation ‘more difficult’ • Macron arrives in Riyadh for ‘surprise solidarity visit’ RIYADH: As the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthi movement continues to escalate, the Saudi-led coalition on Wednesday said it had intercepted six drones launched towards the kingdom, including in the Madina region. “Four drones launched towards the kingdom have been intercepted and destroyed,” coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki posted on X, adding in a second post that the interceptions took place in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern region as well as Madina. Al-Malki, who did not specify who was behind the launches, later said drones had been intercepted, also in the eastern region. The Houthis denied having targeted the kingdom, with military spokesman Yahya Saree saying their forces had not carried out any “deep” operations in Saudi territory. The Saudi energy ministry said that falling debris from the successful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility “resulted in the deaths of two individuals, a Filipino and a Nepali, and injuries to two others”. It did not say who launched the drone aimed at Shaybah oil field near the UAE border. Within Yemen, the Houthis claimed an attack on Wednesday on a military camp near the airport in the southern city of Aden, where the Yemeni government is based. “Our armed forces were able to target the Saudi enemy’s operations room in the Badr camp in Aden with a ballistic missile,” Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said in a statement. A government military source and a local official told Reuters the group also attacked Riyan airport in the southeastern coastal city of Mukalla. “The Houthis used missiles and drones to target a military base housing forces from the Saudi-led coalition at Al Rayyan airport,” one of the officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, told AFP. Saree said the group had targeted “military equipment transported by the Saudi enemy via military cargo planes to Al Rayyan airport”. Egypt to support Saudis Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Wednesday that Cairo’s proposed military support for Riyadh was to “defend Saudi territory, and does not include an attack on Yemen,” state-linked media reported. Al-Qahera News , which is closely linked to state intelligence and is to broadcast a speech by Sisi, reported that he also said “the stability of our brothers in the Gulf concerns Egypt’s national security”. The speech itself has not yet been aired by Wednesday night. Egypt’s parliament on Monday delayed a debate on President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s request to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia until next week. Sisi had asked lawmakers to approve military support for Saudi Arabia if requested by the kingdom, which has come under near-daily attacks from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis. Iran warns against interference However, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that any interference in the Yemen war by Egypt or any other country would make the situation “more difficult”. “Egypt has sufficient experience to avoid entangling itself in such a highly complex conflict,” said Iran’s top diplomat in an interview with Iraqi state broadcaster Al-Iraqiya aired on Tuesday. “We believe that any foreign presence or interference will only make resolving this issue more difficult,” Mr Araghchi noted. He added that Egypt has said it “will not enter Yemen or engage in a war against Yemen”. The decade-plus war between the Iran-backed Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government reignited in July. Macron meets MbS Meanwhile, French President Emmanuel Macron arrived in Riyadh in a surprise “solidarity” visit, and met Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Macron is the first Western leader to visit since the Houthis intensified their attacks on the kingdom this month. The trip is part of a Gulf tour to secure diesel and petrol supplies as Macron seeks to bring down energy prices following violent protests in France sparked by rising living costs that have created a political crisis for the president. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

items.title: Airbnb hosts can no longer make guests strip beds and wash dishes under new rules
items.description: Airbnb has changed its rules to limit what property hosts can ask guests to do—including cleaning. The updated guidelines say hosts can now set seven standard house rules and add other “reasonable” requests. Airbnb states that guests – who are required to pay a cleaning fee – should not be asked to complete tasks normally done by a cleaner, including washing dishes and stripping beds. The new rules will apply to all reservations booked on or after 20 November on the accommodation marketplace. “House rules help guests understand what hosts expect, but we’ve heard from our community that they can be confusing, onerous and hard to manage,” Airbnb told the BBC. “So, we’ve redesigned them to make them easier to discover and clearer to set, alongside a new policy that keeps requests reasonable, with no surprises.” According to the new requirements on the Airbnb website, hosts are generally not allowed to ask guests to complete tasks that “require significant effort or time, or would typically be performed by a cleaner, including stripping the bed, taking trash offsite, or washing and putting away dishes”. The company said it may grant exceptions in some circumstances. For example, guests may be asked to limit shower time if local drought-related water restrictions apply. A property’s rules will be displayed more prominently to guests going forward and will appear in guests’ reservation reminders. Contracts will only be allowed in limited circumstances, including when required by law or homeowners association rules. While a host can’t impose fines, they remain in control of their house rules and requests, the company said. If a host’s request does not follow Airbnb policies, the issue will be flagged, and the owner can appeal if they disagree. Guests have long complained about unreasonable tasks they must complete before departure, especially since they pay cleaning fees. TikTok videos from Airbnb hosts Cassie and Jon, who show them closely inspecting their rental property in the US state of Georgia after guests leave, have recently gone viral for their attention to detail. One video, for example, accuses guests of “disrespecting the house rules” for leaving a television remote out of place. They have been criticised for their strict rules and high standards but said in response that their content had been misinterpreted Their videos have inspired other content creators to parody stringent hosts.

items.description: Salman Akram Raja • Raja ‘rebukes’ move by KP lawmakers to nominate Gandapur as interim KP president • Ex-CM fires back, demands apology from secy gen over ‘name-calling’ PESHAWAR: The debacle that befell the PTI’s recent protest march has led to serious fissures within the core committee, with demands emerging from within for chan­ges at the leadership level that can steer the party out of its current crisis. The bad blood became public on Wednesday as two senior party leaders — Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and former KP chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur — traded accusations of betraying the party cause. Meanwhile, a woman parliamentarian from Peshawar echoed the sentiments of many within the core committee when she demanded accountability over the failure of the party’s much-touted protest march, which resulted in the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, and created more problems for their jailed leader, Imran Khan. The Salman Akram-Ali Amin spat on X (formerly Twitter) followed reports that a group of lawmakers from the KP Assembly had met to endorse the latter’s nomination as acting provincial president in place of MNA Junaid Akbar, who has been missing since the imposition of governor’s rule. The handwritten text, addressed to interim party chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and seen by Dawn , said that the meeting “unanimously” proposed to nominate Mr Gandapur as the acting provincial president in the absence of Junaid Akbar, calling the ex-CM “the right man for the right job”. The Oct 14 meeting, which according to one participant was held via Zoom and WhatsApp, was attended by around 55 provincial lawmakers. Their four-pronged agenda included party organisation issues; the status of negotiations with the government; the party’s plan for further protests; and legal issues. The main outcome that invited derision from Mr Raja, however, was the resolution demanding that Mr Gandapur be appointed the acting provincial president immediately. This prompted the secretary general to take a dig at “the narrative” regarding a possible announcement by a group of party MPAs, nominating a new provincial president without permission from their jailed leader Imran Khan, or the party’s political committee. He put the number of these dissidents at 68. Ali Amin Gandapur The secretary general accused the group of cutting off contact with Sohail Afridi and his team in the final days of the protest march, paving the way for state coercion, emergency and governor’s rule in the province. He asserted that Ali Asghar, the party’s provincial general secretary, remained the acting provincial head and Mr Afridi continued to be the chief minister, in accordance with the law and Constitution. “Those spreading doubts — the snakes and the serpents — will be defeated,” he wrote while concluding his post on X. Subsequently, an angry Mr Gandapur took to X to hit back at the secretary general’s claims; in a series of tweets and audio messages, he took strong exception to Mr Raja’s tone and tenor. Demanding that he bring to an end “the spectacle” that had been made of the party, the former KP CM said that the secretary general had no right to accuse others of conspiracy, or call them names like “snakes and serpents”. “Do you understand this? We know how to make others understand if they don’t get this,” he said in an angry tone. Accusing Mr Raja of “hiding” during the party’s protest movement, he asked what sacrifices he had rendered for the party, and demanded the secretary general apologise for his remarks. “At a time when the party is facing unprecedented political challenges, levelling vague accusations and using mocking language against your own elected representatives does not befit responsible leadership,” he wrote on X. “I don’t know who has fed Salman Akram Raja and what the purpose of his tweet was”, Mr Gandapur continued. He also wondered why Mr Raja and Barrister Gohar did not attend parliamentary party meetings, despite repeated invitations to discuss the fallout of the decisions they had taken, which had brought the party to this juncture. “If the parliamentary party of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa wants to seek a constitutional and political solution to the current crisis through consultation within itself, who has given a few individuals the authority to label these elected representatives as traitors, conspirators, or undemocratic?” Incidentally, this is not the first time that both men have taken to social media to air their internal party grievances. In 2025, ahead of a nationwide protest, Mr Gandapur and then-PTI Punjab organiser Aliya Hamza Malik had become embroiled in a similar argument over social media. At the time, the argument had prompted a censure from the jailed party founder, who had strictly instructed senior officeholders and junior members alike to avoid expressing “internal differences on social media, electronic media, print media, or any other platform”. “Publicly airing internal matters or individual concerns before the media is entirely unacceptable,” Imran Khan had said at the time. The latest exchange between the two party leaders also harkened to an outburst from MPA Mashal Yousafzai — former spokesperson to Bushra Bibi — who has blamed the former chief minister and a few other party leaders for the failure of the protest march and subsequent imposition of governor’s rule. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

items.title: ‘Who builds schools to teach people how to use WhatsApp?’ – Bright Simons
items.description: Vice-President and head of Research at the IMANI Centre for Policy and Education, Bright Simons, has urged policymakers to remove barriers that keep ordinary Ghanaians from benefiting from digital technology. Speaking at Joy News’ Digital Economy Forum on AI and the Ghana Economy on Wednesday, he challenged the assumption that people always need organised training to use digital platforms productively. “Who builds schools to teach people how to use WhatsApp? Who builds schools to teach influencers how to do YouTube influencing?” he asked. Mr Simons pointed to ride-hailing, e-commerce and delivery services as examples of how ordinary people have acquired useful digital skills through practical use. “Nobody taught them how to use mapping services. There were very few attempts to do that. Somehow we figured out how to use mapping services, how to do geolocation and deliver food and the rest of it.” His argument centred on policy’s role in creating opportunities. Removing obstacles, he said, can be a practical way to help people earn a living from technology. “So we have to think about policy as also including the things that remove barriers and bottlenecks for ordinary people,” he said. He warned that government intervention could itself become an obstacle to adopting digital services. “I’m a big believer in the fact that when it comes to those kinds of things, typically the government is an impediment rather than an enabler.” Mr Simons recalled resisting proposals to license Uber, Bolt and other ride-hailing services. He said the proposals included onerous local government obligations. He also cited the public uproar over developer licensing as a reason to scrutinise new regulatory requirements before introducing them. For him, discussions about such rules directly affect ordinary people. They determine whether digital opportunities become easier or harder to access. He rejected the idea that identifying policy barriers is a theoretical exercise. “Often they are impediments and bottlenecks in their way, and people like us who point them out should not be seen as discussing theory. It’s very practical.”

items.title: Pakistan, Qatar, Turkiye and Indonesia sign 'Badr' defence cooperation pact
items.description: Pakistan, Qatar, Turkiye and Indonesia on Wednesday signed a multilateral pact to promote cooperation in defence production and capabilities, the Turkish defence ministry said. The signing took place in Qatar, with ministers of the four countries attending the ceremony. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif represented Pakistan at the signing. The Foreign Office has yet to comment on the signing of the defence pact, but Asif posted on X his “key statements” on the ‘Badr Memorandum of Understanding’ (MoU). The remarks were posted as a visual share, which said: “Pakistan places great importance on strengthening defence cooperation with trusted partners. This memorandum reflects Islamabad’s shared commitment to contributing to regional peace and stability. “We look forward to exploring opportunities for strengthening self-reliance, industrial collaboration, joint production and technology transfer while drawing on the complementary strengths of our respective defence industries, in accordance with relevant international and domestic laws and regulations.” The statement further said, “Through this partnership, we aim to advance cooperation across joint research and development, training exchanges and industrial capability building.” Turkiye and Qatar released similar statements on the signing of the pact. Reuters quoted the Turkish ministry as saying that the pact, titled ‘Badr Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)’, was aimed at defence cooperation and strengthening defensive capabilities. “The agreement holds substantial economic importance,” it said, adding the accord sought to foster cooperation in military production, boost military capabilities, and help collaboration in technical military training, research and development. “By leveraging the unique military production capabilities of each country, the initiative will facilitate cooperation and integration, enhance defence industrial capacities, and enable the fulfilment of the needs of allied and friendly nations,” it added. Later, the Qatari defence ministry also released a similar statement. Turkish Defence Minister Yaşar Güler, Qatar’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of State for Defence Sheikh Saud bin Abdulrahman, and Indonesia’s Deputy Minister of Defence Yusuf Jauhari were the other signatories. Haluk Görgün, who heads Turkiye’s Secretariat of Defence Industries , was also present on the occasion. Görgün said in a statement that the accord formed the foundation of a “strategic cooperation” to develop joint production and technology. “Technology sharing, joint development and strengthening domestic production capabilities lie at the heart of sustainable defence industry. As Turkiye, we value partnerships that go beyond off-the-shelf procurement models, that foster the development of a nation’s own human capital and industrial infrastructure,” Gorgun said. “We believe that the Badr MoU will contribute to transforming the complementary capabilities of Qatar, Pakistan, Indonesia, and Turkiye into concrete projects,” he added. State-run Qatar News Agency said the pact was named ‘Badr’, “referring to the full moon, to signify how the four nations complement one another through this agreement, given its immense importance in terms of both defence and the economy”. “Other friendly nations may join the MoU, in accordance with criteria agreed upon by the four countries,” it said. Pakistan has strong brotherly and historic ties with the three countries, with intense diplomatic engagement seen in recent months with Qatar and Turkiye particularly. Pakistan and Turkiye, along with Saudi Arabia, are members of the Makkah Defence Alliance , under which they are to treat an attack against any of them as an attack against all. Qatar had welcomed that pact as cooperation aimed at regional security and stability. Islamabad and Doha have remained engaged as mediators in the US-Iran war. Meanwhile, Pakistan and Turkiye are part of the Regional Four (R4) Group along with Saudi Arabia and Egypt, which emerged in March and has met several times since then. Earlier this week, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met his Qatari counterpart during his visit to Doha, where the two agreed to boost bilateral cooperation in internal security. During his November 2025 visit to the Gulf state, President Asif Ali Zardari met with Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and offered to expand bilateral cooperation in the areas of defence production. Last month, Indonesian naval chief Admiral Dr Muhammad Ali called on Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir in Rawalpindi. The two sides “reaffirmed their resolve to further strengthen cooperation, particularly in the domains of professional training, defence collaboration and joint exercises”, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said. The naval chief had also met President Asif Ali Zardari. In January, Defence Minister retired Lieutenant General Sjafrie Sjamsoeddin had called on CDF Munir, with ISPR saying he expressed Jakarta’s desire to further expand defence ties with Pakistan.

items.title: Crystal Palace urged to retire bald eagle mascot
items.description: An animal rights group is urging Crystal Palace to retire its live bald eagle mascot immediately, saying a “bright stadium filled with boisterous fans is no place for animals”. In a letter to Palace CEO Sharon Lacey, People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) asked the Premier League club to stop using the eagle, named Phoenix, in pre-match displays at Selhurst Park and to never use live animal mascots again. The London team, known as the Eagles since 1973, introduced a live eagle to matchdays in 2010. Kayla, who died in 2020, performed the role for 10 years, and her replacement, Phoenix, made her debut against West Ham in August 2024. Peta says birds can become “frightened, disoriented and panicked” in stadium environments, putting themselves and fans at risk. Using them for displays and entertainment also denies the animals, who “would naturally avoid humans”, the opportunity to engage with their natural instincts, leading to “frustration and stress”, the group said. The organisation has “detailed records” of incidents involving live mascots, including birds, being injured or killed in collisions with walls, windows and match balls, as well as a falcon embedding its talons in a spectator’s scalp after landing on his head. In 2017, a Charlton Athletic fan was found guilty of trying to punch Kayla the eagle at a League Cup fixture two years earlier. “Many professional sports teams use only willing humans as mascots, and the club already has Pete the Eagle to excite the crowd,” said Dr Carys Bennett, Peta’s senior corporate projects manager. “Bald eagles are widely recognised as symbols of freedom. They deserve better than to be used as an entertainment prop to amuse the Eagles’ fans.” BBC Sport has contacted Crystal Palace for comment.

items.title: PSG’s Kvaratskhelia to undergo surgery for a ruptured ACL
items.description: Paris Saint-Germain winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will undergo knee surgery after rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) during his side’s 4-2 win over Barcelona on Tuesday. Kvaratskhelia sustained the injury during a challenge with Xavi Espart and couldn’t put weight on his right leg, so he was substituted in the 59th minute of the Champions League tie. PSG have not put a timeline on his return to action. In a statement on Instagram, Kvaratskhelia said: “Before every game I play, I ask God to leave the field healthy, but in vain. “I probably prepared for this game the best I have ever prepared for. I thought I was prepared for everything. “I realise that God chose me and if I protected the players on another field, I’m ready to go through these months of hard work, pain, tears. “I know I have to come back stronger for my people who always have my back. I won’t let you down, I promise, I won’t waste a second.” Kvaratskhelia, 25, helped PSG win back-to-back Champions League titles after moving from Napoli to the French capital in January 2025. The Georgia international has featured 11 times for PSG this season. The club also confirmed Ousmane Dembele and Marquinhos will be absent for a “few weeks”. Dembele limped off with a left thigh injury while Marquinhos injured his right thigh. PSG and Barcelona were level at 2-2 heading into the final 10 minutes at Parc des Princes before the hosts scored twice late on to maintain their winning start to their Champions League defence. They sit top of the table with three wins from three matches.

items.title: Fernandes rounds on Carrick after Man Utd humiliation
items.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes turned on head coach Michael Carrick after one of the club’s most humiliating nights in European history. A 4-1 Champions League hammering at Como put Carrick’s future in the spotlight. He apologised to the 700 travelling fans, having ignored his beaten players after the final whistle to march across the pitch and repeatedly hold his hands up – in a manner similar to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer following a 4-1 defeat at Watford in November 2021, which led to his dismissal as United boss 24 hours later. However, Fernandes, widely seen as a football obsessive who watches games regularly and understands the tactical side as well as any player in the United squad, inflicted more damage when he spoke to TNT Sports afterwards. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much of the ball to these teams they get confidence,” he said. Asked directly whether Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes added: “That’s on the manager and staff to see it, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.” Told of Fernandes’ comments in his post-match press conference, Carrick offered a curt response: “There’s a little bit of whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you aren’t going to win.” Carrick avoids questions on future, apologises to fans for unacceptable display Carrick also refused to answer questions about his own future. Instead, he described his own feelings about United’s performance and focused on taking responsibility. “I have to apologise to the supporters,” said the former player. “I care about this football club as much as anyone, if not more, with the position that I’m in and what I value this football club. For us to play in that way is not acceptable. “I always go over to the fans anyway, regardless, so it wasn’t a particularly different kind of reason why I went over. “It’s the appreciation and acknowledgement of what they’ve gone through and have done over a period of a few weeks now. As I said, I was one of them. “I’m feeling the same as them. We’ve got a lot of values in this football club; what we represent and how we want to go about it. We might win, we might lose, but the way we went about it tonight wasn’t acceptable. I just wanted the fans to know I feel for them. “Listen. I’ve not given my own position any thought — this is for the supporters. I was one of them watching that, and I wasn’t happy at all.” Seven without a win – Man Utd’s bleak picture After winning 12 of his 17 games in charge last season to guide United back into the Champions League after a two-year absence, Carrick was given a two-year contract. However, as happened with Solskjaer five years ago, the new campaign has unravelled spectacularly and they are 13th in the Premier League, three points clear of bottom club Sunderland. Although they recovered from their shock opening-day defeat to newly promoted Hull by coming from behind to beat Ipswich the following week, United have not won in the Premier League since. Their only other success in 11 games in all competitions came against Azerbaijan champions Sabah FK in the Champions League. Their latest loss meant they have now gone seven games without a win, their worst run since they went eight without a victory under Louis van Gaal between 25 November and 28 December 2015. Only Joshua Zirkzee’s injury-time consolation kept United from suffering their joint second-worst European defeat ever. The embarrassment was heightened by the knowledge that when they were last crowned European champions in 2008, Como were playing semi-professional football in front of a couple of hundred spectators in Serie D. It is a basic reality that if Como’s star man, Nico Paz, who opened the scoring after 118 seconds, scored a second and a third goal, and said he wanted to leave Como, virtually every big club in Europe would want to sign him, and United’s chances would be virtually non-existent. They entertain 15th-placed Bournemouth in the Premier League on Sunday, knowing that before last season’s amazing 4-4 draw, the Cherries won 3-0 on their previous two visits to Old Trafford. What happens now? Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick acknowledges the club’s fans after the 4-1 defeat by Como United flew straight back to Manchester after the game. It remains to be seen whether the position around Carrick changes before the Bournemouth game. However, United supporters sang against the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe as the shambolic evening unravelled. Both Carrick and sporting director Jason Wilcox have been absolved of partial blame for the club’s plight by some; Carrick because he was let down badly in the summer transfer window, when the club signed three midfielders, but failed to bring in competition for Luke Shaw at left-back and Benjamin Sesko in attack. Wilcox too, because he had to work to a budget set by those above him, including chief executive Omar Berrada. “There was a lot going through my mind watching that,” admitted Carrick, who won five Premier League titles and the Champions League during his United playing career. “It was tough to watch. “It wasn’t just the goals, if I’m totally honest. It was was the manner and way we played at times. “I’m giving my absolute best all the time, I care about it. My whole life is wrapped around it. It might go well, it might not go so well, but I I genuinely give everything that I possibly can.”

items.title: Chinese Premier Li Qiang meets with Russian President Vladimir Putin
items.description: Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Wednesday that against the backdrop of a continuously evolving and complex international situation, China and Russia have maintained close coordination, serving as a valuable force for stability in a world marked by turbulence and transformation. Li made the remarks during a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg. Li first conveyed cordial greetings and best wishes from Chinese President Xi Jinping to Putin, noting that since the beginning of this year, the two heads of state have met twice and made further plans to deepen China-Russia relations and cooperation. China is willing to work with Russia to strengthen strategic communication, consolidate political mutual trust, expand all-round mutually beneficial cooperation, and continuously enhance the well-being of the two peoples, he said. Li noted that China is ready to work with Russia to better leverage their economic complementarity, maintain the sound momentum of bilateral cooperation, strengthen practical cooperation in energy and resources, trade and investment, transportation and other areas, deliver more positive outcomes and promote common prosperity in both countries. The two sides should ensure the success of the China-Russia Years of Education, continuously deepen exchanges and cooperation in culture, tourism, sports and youth, and further enhance mutual understanding and friendship between the two peoples, Li said. Noting that unilateralism and hegemonism are rampant in today's world, Li said China is ready to strengthen communication and coordination with Russia on major issues, enhance coordination within multilateral platforms such as the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and BRICS, unite more forces of the Global South to safeguard common interests and uphold fairness and justice. Putin asked Li to convey his sincere greetings to Xi and wished the upcoming fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China success. Putin said that he and Xi had met several times this year and reached new important consensus on advancing the Russia-China comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination for a new era. Since the establishment of the Russia-China prime ministers' regular meeting mechanism 30 years ago, it has earnestly implemented the achievements of head-of-state diplomacy and promoted the deepening and substantive cooperation between the two sides, Putin said. Russia-China relations are built on the basis of equality and mutual respect, mutual benefit and win-win results, and accommodation of each other's concerns, he said, noting that bilateral relations are not affected by changes in the international landscape and not subject to interference from any third party. China has been and will always be Russia's closest and most reliable partner, Putin noted. Russia is ready to work with China to deepen practical cooperation in the areas of energy, agriculture, space, civilian nuclear energy, information technology, artificial intelligence and transportation, to jointly ensure the success of the Russia-China Years of Education, and to expand people-to-people and cultural exchanges, he said. Putin added that Russia supports China in hosting the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting this year and in assuming the BRICS chairmanship next year.

items.title: Solve local problems before taking on global giants — Zipline director
items.description: Ghanaian entrepreneurs should focus on solving specific local problems and build businesses around their competitive advantages instead of attempting to compete directly with established global companies, the Country Director of Zipline Ghana, Mr Daniel Kwaku Merki, has said. He said a strategy of starting small, developing solutions tailored to local conditions and expanding gradually could help Ghanaian startups build resilient businesses capable of withstanding competition from international firms. Speaking at the JoyNews Digital Economy Forum on AI and the Ghana Economy on Wednesday, October 21, Mr Merki said local businesses needed to identify what distinguished them from their competitors and use that advantage as the foundation for growth. Drawing on his experience as an entrepreneur and early-stage investor, he cautioned against trying to compete immediately at a scale that favoured larger, better-resourced companies. “If you go too high up, what happens is you will fail,” he said, adding that businesses needed to identify a narrow problem they could solve better than others before expanding their operations. “You cannot just jump and go and compete with somebody who has all the advantages. You have to find your source of differentiation, go small and solve something very narrowly and then scale up,” he said. Local knowledge as a competitive advantage Mr Merki said Ghanaian businesses could draw strength from their understanding of local markets, including the informal systems and practices that foreign companies might struggle to replicate. He cited a logistics and fulfilment company in Ghana in which he had invested, saying its ability to integrate technology with the realities of the local market could give it an advantage over a global competitor such as Amazon if the latter entered the market. “What happens to that company when Amazon wants to enter the market, if they do it the right way, Amazon cannot compete in this market because there are certain things that work even in the informal sector that you have to leverage the technology, integrate and make that the core,” he said. His comments point to the need for Ghanaian technology businesses to develop solutions that respond to local conditions rather than simply imitate business models that have succeeded elsewhere. For startups seeking to use artificial intelligence (AI), that could mean identifying specific challenges in areas such as logistics, commerce and service delivery, then applying technology in ways that improve existing systems and meet the needs of local customers. Government’s role While emphasising the importance of entrepreneurship and private-sector innovation, Mr Merki said government also had a responsibility to establish the conditions needed for businesses to grow. He welcomed the emphasis on a long-term national strategy for the digital economy, saying entrepreneurs needed to see ambition and a clear direction in the country’s plans. “What matters to me is that I see that there is a strategy that is 10 years out, that there is ambition,” he said. Mr Merki referred to a target in the strategy for Ghana to produce 10 unicorns by 2035, adding that he believed the country could achieve an even higher number. A unicorn is a privately held startup valued at US$1 billion or more. Reaching that milestone typically requires businesses to develop scalable products, attract investment and demonstrate strong growth potential. Mr Merki’s remarks underscore the importance of combining a clear national vision with practical support for entrepreneurs, particularly those developing technology-driven solutions for Ghanaian markets. He said the government’s role was distinct from that of private businesses, but the development of a competitive digital economy required a collective effort.

items.title: Ouagadougou : poursuivi pour usage d’un faux billet, un vendeur ambulant de 19 ans relaxé
items.description: Un vendeur ambulant de dix-neuf ans, poursuivi pour usage d’un faux billet de dix mille francs CFA, a été relaxé par le Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) Ouaga I, après un court séjour à la Maison d’arrêt et de correction de Ouagadougou (MACO). Cette affaire montre comment l’ignorance ou un geste en apparence banal peut parfois conduire derrière les barreaux. Un jeune vendeur ambulant a comparu le 23 septembre 2026 devant le TGI Ouaga I. Malgré l’absence de micro, qui rendait les échanges difficiles à suivre, l’AIB a pu noter que le prévenu, A. O., vend des sacs à cinq mille francs CFA l’unité. Au cours de l’une de ses tournées, il est tombé sur un autre commerçant, visiblement âgé, qui proposait des maillots. Nous le désignerons par les initiales S. A. « Il est venu vers moi et il m’a dit qu’il voulait une tenue. Je lui ai répondu que ça coûtait 2 500 F CFA, et il a tenté de m’expliquer qu’il ne comprenait pas le mooré », a relaté cet homme à la silhouette svelte, qui a comparu en qualité de. A. O. lui aurait tendu le billet de dix mille francs CFA sans discuter. Constatant qu’il s’agissait d’une contrefaçon, S. A. aurait d’abord froissé le billet, avant de menacer de le déchirer. Le prévenu lui aurait demandé de ne pas le faire. Le commerçant aurait ensuite conduit le jeune homme vers un agent de police qui se trouvait à proximité. A. O. a par la suite été conduit dans un commissariat de la ville, puis placé sous mandat de dépôt à la MACO. Interrogé par le tribunal, S. A. a estimé que A. O. était innocent. Selon lui, le jeune vendeur avait lui-même été trompé par un client indélicat qui lui aurait acheté deux sacs. Dans son réquisitoire, le procureur du Faso a relevé qu’il était difficile de prouver que le prévenu avait utilisé la coupure en connaissance de cause. Tenant compte également du fait qu’il comparaissait pour la première fois, il a requis sa relaxe. « Le tribunal a décidé de te laisser partir. Tu seras libéré aujourd’hui. Ou bien tu veux rester avec nous ? Posez-lui la question », a déclaré le président du tribunal à l’interprète du prévenu, qui semblait s’exprimer en langue peule. Sans hésiter, A. O. a choisi la liberté, sourire aux lèvres et l’air soulagé. « Maintenant, il faut aller vendre de la viande grillée et tu laisses les sacs », a lancé le président du tribunal, sur le ton de la plaisanterie. Agence d’information du Burkina ZS/ata L’article Ouagadougou : poursuivi pour usage d’un faux billet, un vendeur ambulant de 19 ans relaxé est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Frais universitaires : Critiquant le maintien d'El Midaoui, les étudiants salariés se mobilisent devant le Parlement
items.description: La Coordination nationale des fonctionnaires et des salariés soumis au régime des horaires aménagés a annoncé une nouvelle étape dans sa mobilisation contre les frais universitaires imposés aux étudiants salariés. Elle prévoit un sit-in nocturne devant le Parlement mercredi 21 octobre, à partir de 19 heures, suivi d’un rassemblement de protestation jeudi 22 octobre, à 11 heures, au même endroit. Dans un communiqué, la coordination a vivement critiqué le maintien d’Azzedine El Midaoui à la tête du ministère de l’enseignement supérieur. Elle estime que sa gestion du dossier des frais imposés aux étudiants salariés a contribué à aggraver la crise, en prolongeant une approche qu’elle juge inadaptée, sans qu’aucune issue ne soit trouvée à l’impasse actuelle. Pour les représentants de la coordination, la persistance de cette situation traduit une incapacité à s’attaquer aux causes profondes du problème. « Reproduire la crise au lieu d’en éliminer les causes ne constitue pas une manière de remédier aux dysfonctionnements, mais revient à en pérenniser les effets », dénonce le communiqué. La Coordination ajoute que la suspension des droits au nom des procédures administratives constitue une forme de temporisation déguisée, qui vide le principe d’égalité des chances de sa substance et porte atteinte à la gratuité de l’enseignement supérieur. La coordination met également en cause la responsabilité politique de la cheffe du gouvernement dans le maintien de cette situation. Elle l’appelle à assumer les conséquences de la décision relative à ces frais et à y mettre définitivement fin. Selon elle, ces prélèvements contribuent à renforcer l’exclusion universitaire et à soumettre le droit à l’éducation aux contraintes du marché et aux capacités financières des étudiants. L’organisation juge ainsi contradictoire de revendiquer une volonté de réforme tout en maintenant les facteurs à l’origine de la crise. Elle estime, en outre, que les personnes lésées ne sauraient être les seules à supporter les conséquences de l’incapacité des autorités à trouver une solution. C’est dans ce contexte que la coordination entend intensifier sa mobilisation, tout en affirmant privilégier une démarche pacifique et organisée. Le sit-in nocturne prévu mercredi, à partir de 19 heures, puis le rassemblement de jeudi à 11 heures devant le Parlement, visent à défendre la gratuité de l’enseignement supérieur et à obtenir réparation pour les étudiants concernés. items.title: ABUAD decorates United Nigeria Airlines, Cavista Holdings chairmen with honorary degrees
items.description: …as varsity graduates 2,194 students at 14th convocation …as Canadian, US universities decorate Afe Babalola with honorary law degrees By Rotimi Ojomoyela Ado-Ekiti–Afe Babalola University, Ado-Ekiti (ABUAD), has conferred honorary degrees of Doctor of Letters (D.Litt.) on the Chairmen of United Nigeria Airlines and Cavista Holdings, Professor Obiora Okonkwo and Niyi Olajide, in recognition of their contributions to business development, innovation and national growth. The honours were bestowed on the two distinguished personalities at the university’s 14th convocation ceremony, which featured the graduation of 2,194 students and brought together prominent political leaders, traditional rulers, business executives and other distinguished personalities. Personalities at the convocation include the Governor of Ekiti State, Biodun Oyebanji, Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Enitan Ogunwusi, Ojaja II; the Ewi of Ado-Ekiti, Oba Rufus Adejugbe; the Ogoga of Ikere-Ekiti, Oba Samuel Adu Adejimi and the Olowo of Owo Kingdom, Oba Ajibade Gbadegesin Ogunoye III. Others are the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN; Dr Wole Oluyede, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ekiti State; Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN; and former Governor of Ekiti State, Engr Segun Oni. Speaking at the convocation ceremony, the Governor of Ekiti State, Biodun Oyebanji hailed Olajide for his investments in agriculture, tourism and other sectors of Ekiti State’s economy, while Okonkwo was recognised for his contributions to business and enterprise development. He also described the duo as accomplished international entrepreneurs who had complemented the state government’s drive to attract private investment, generate employment and accelerate industrialisation. The governor said Olajide, through Cavista Holdings, the parent company of Agbeyewa Farms and Glocient Hospitality, had committed millions of dollars to the state’s economy, with significant investments in agriculture, hospitality and tourism. He also added that Professor Obiora’s investment in aviation, made it possible for Ekiti State to record over 10,000 passengers at the Ekiti Cargo Allied International Airport since the commencement of the commercial flights in December 10, 2025. “I want to sincerely extend the same congratulatory message to my brother, Mr. John Niyi Olajide, an accomplished innovator, international businessman and a passionate Ekiti compatriot. Even though, he has made good fortunes for himself abroad, he has joined in the vision of our government to promote private investment and industrialize the State. “Through his Cavista Holdings, the parent owners of Agbeyewa Farms and Glocient Hospitality, he has invested millions of dollars in Ekiti economy, employing hundreds of people and transforming both the agriculture and tourism landscape of Ekiti State. He is in charge of the ongoing transformation of Ikogosi Warm Spring Resorts to a world class tourist destination. “Today, Niyi John Olajide is the second biggest investor in Ekiti after Aare Afe Babalola. His investments through Cavista Holdings has employed thousands of Ekiti people through his investment in Agbeyewa Farms, the biggest cassava farm in the world and through his transformative impact at Ikogosi Warm Spring that has turned the corridor to the world renowned Holiday Resort in Nigeria”. He added The Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, also praised the duo’s achievements, describing them as outstanding personalities whose commitment to job creation and entrepreneurship deserve recognition. The Ewi of Ado-Ekiti, Oba Rufus Adejugbe, called for greater private-sector participation in the state’s development, noting that Ekiti needed more entrepreneurs willing to commit their resources, expertise and experience to building its economy. The monarch said the state had long looked forward to attracting more investors to complement the developmental contributions of ABUAD founder, Aare Afe Babalola. Other highlight of the event was the conferment of honorary Doctor of Laws degrees on the founder of the University, Aare Afe Babalola by the representatives of Trinity Western University, Canada, and Trinity International University, United States, for his contributions in several sector such as education, health, law, agriculture, among others In his remarks, Aare Afe Babalola described the convocation as the best moment of his life, urging the graduating students to be good ambassadors of the university and become problem solvers. In their responses, the honorees commended the contributions of Aare Afe Babalola towards the development of the state and the country, with a pledge to continue to use their goodwills for the development of Ekiti and Nigeria at large. Giving the breakdown of the 2,194 graduands, 1,759 completed undergraduate and professional programmes, while 435 agraduated from postgraduate programmes, comprising 359 students of the College of Postgraduate Studies and 76 from the ABUAD Business School’s postgraduate programmes. 286 graduands obtained First Class degrees, while 824 earned Second Class Upper degrees. Another 234 obtained Second Class Lower degrees, while 29 graduated with Third Class degrees. The remaining graduands completed professional or postgraduate programmes to which the conventional degree classifications do not apply. The post ABUAD decorates United Nigeria Airlines, Cavista Holdings chairmen with honorary degrees appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Draft auto policy revs up hopes for cheaper vehicles
items.description: • PHEVs may see price reductions of over 20pc under proposed tax changes • Petrol, hybrid vehicles may become around 8-10pc cheaper • Parts makers warn rising CBU imports, lower tariffs to hurt local industry KARACHI: The draft Auto Policy 2026-31 could trigger one of the biggest shake-ups in the country’s automobile market, with prices of some vehicles potentially falling by more than 20 per cent. However, the prospect of cheaper cars may create an unusual predicament, as buyers are likely to hold back purchases in anticipation of lower prices, causing anxiety among automakers over the value of their existing inventory. According to Topline Securities, the new draft maintains the 1pc general sales tax (GST) rate on battery electric vehicles (BEVs), while setting rates at 9pc for plug-in hybrid vehicles (PHEVs) and 6pc for range-extended electric vehicles (REEVs). The earlier draft had proposed a uniform 1pc GST across all new energy vehicles (NEVs), while the previous policy imposed rates of 8.5pc to 12.75pc on PHEVs. This points to the government’s priority to incentivise the rollout of NEVs, particularly BEVs. Preliminary industry estimates suggest conventional petrol vehicles could become approximately 8-10pc cheaper, while hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) may see reductions of around 9pc. PHEVs could benefit even more, with estimated price reductions exceeding 20pc. Among BEVs, models with import values below $15,000 could see reductions of approximately 22pc compared to around 8pc for higher-priced BEVs. However, REEVs may become around 3pc more expensive under the proposed tax structure. The new draft proposes reducing tariffs on localised completely knocked-down (CKD) parts to 15pc by FY31 from 25pc previously. Topline Securities said the reduction could be detrimental to the local vendor industry, adding that the benefits were likely to be passed on to consumers amid intense competition. Parts makers sound alarm Pakistan Association of Automotive Parts and Accessories Manufacturers (PAPAAM) Chairman Abdur Rehman Aizaz said the new auto policy amounted to a “conspiracy to destroy several industries”. He said rising imports of new and used cars were already hurting the developed local auto parts industry, which now faced the threat of closures because of government policies. Mr Aizaz pointed out that imports of completely built-up (CBU) new cars rose to 2,407 units in September from 391 in August, while imports of used cars increased to 2,454 units from 1,185 over the same period. He said every new or used imported vehicle reduced potential volumes for the country’s 1,200 local auto parts manufacturers. Locally produced parts accounted for approximately Rs1.5 million of the value of each domestically assembled vehicle, he added. On that basis, the 4,861 CBU vehicles imported in September represented an estimated Rs7.3 billion in lost revenue for local parts manufacturers, Mr Aizaz said. Industry representatives said the GAC Aion UT, currently priced at around Rs6.4m, could fall to Rs5m-Rs5.2m. Higher-priced electric SUVs such as the BYD Atto 3 and GAC Aion V, priced at around Rs9m, could also see meaningful reductions. They said popular petrol and hybrid models could become more affordable as well. Industry estimates indicate potential savings of around Rs600,000 to Rs800,000 on selected variants of the Honda HR-V e:HEV, Haval Jolion and Toyota Corolla Altis. The biggest absolute reductions could emerge in the PHEV segment. A Jaecoo J7 PHEV, priced near Rs10m, could potentially fall to around Rs8m, while the Kia Sorento PHEV, which has already witnessed substantial price adjustments, could face further downward pressure from changes in GST and import duties. Sania Irfan of Topline Securities said the new draft proposed a zero per cent automotive development levy (ADL) on fossil fuel-driven vehicles below 1,000cc, 2pc on 1,000-2,000cc vehicles and 10pc on those above 2,000cc, replacing the earlier draft’s rates of 4.5-5.5pc across engine categories. Kalbe Ali in Islamabad also contributed to this report Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

items.title: PTI asks govt to ‘rebuild trust’ if it is serious about talks
items.description: • Demands reversal of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa emergency measures, release of political prisoners and Imran’s access to his personal physicians • Claims party’s ‘popularity’ still intact despite ‘coercion’ ISLAMABAD: The PTI on Wednesday called on the government to take confidence-building measures (CBMs) to pave the way for meaningful dialogue, demanding the reversal of what it described as “unlawful” measures, restoration of its provincial government’s mandate in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and release of political prisoners. In a statement, PTI Central Infor­mation Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said meaningful negotiations required concrete action rather than political statements. “If the government was genuinely serious about dialogue, it should take steps to build trust,” he added. Mr Akram demanded the reversal of measures the party considered unlawful, restoration of its provincial government’s mandate and release of political prisoners whose continued detention, he said, could not be legally justified. He also called for the protection of PTI founder Imran Khan’s constitutional and fundamental rights, including lawful meetings with his lawyers and family, fair and timely proceedings in his and his wife’s cases, and medical treatment under the supervision of his personal physicians in accordance with applicable court orders. Mr Akram condemned raids on homes, detentions and pressure on elected representatives and party workers in Punjab and KP, alleging that these actions were intended to intimidate political opponents. PTI’s ‘popularity’ Rejecting Information Minister Attaullah Tarar’s remarks about the party’s political standing, Mr Akram challenged all ruling coalition parties to contest elections against the PTI under a single banner. He said they would suffer a “crushing defeat in a free and fair contest, even today”. On Tuesday, Mr Tarar had said a formal ban on the PTI was no longer needed after the imposition of governor’s rule and an emergency in KP, arguing that the party had “lost po­­w­er” in the province because of security and counterterrorism failures. Mr Akram said the government’s use of “coercive measures and political pressure” had failed to diminish the PTI’s public support. He described the party as Pakistan’s “leading federal political force” and its founder, Imran Khan, as the “only leader enjoying widespread public support across the country”. Rejecting governor’s rule and the emergency in KP, he described the measures as an “attempt to undermine the province’s electoral mandate”. He said the party’s strength stemmed from its connection with the people rather than its control of government offices. He added that no “handpicked administration should be allowed to dictate” the political future of around 50 million residents without respecting their democratic choices and constitutional rights. Mr Akram insisted that decisions concerning the province’s governance, resources, and future must involve its elected representatives and local population. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026

items.title: ‘Journalist safety laws only on paper due to weak complaint systems’
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s laws ai­­m­­ed at protecting journalists from threats and attacks risk remaining largely “on paper” unless the federal and provincial safety commissions are given more powers, accessible complaint mechanisms and the resources needed to deliver timely protection, says a new report released by Freedom Network, a media watchdog, on Wednesday. The report, titled “From safety on paper to safety in practice”, is an as­­s­essment of the work carried out by two commissions — one appointed by the federal government and the other by the Sindh government. The Islamabad-based Freedom Network produced the research with assistance from the International Media Support (IMS). Authored by Minahil Shahab and Adnan Rehmat, the report examined the commissions’ capacity and operational constraints through consultations with stakeholders, interviews and a baseline online survey of around 40 working journalists in Sindh, including respondents from the province’s rural areas. According to report, 65pc of respondents say they have faced work-related threats or interference According to the report, parliament enacted two special laws to combat impunity for crimes against journalists and the media in 2022. Both the federal and Sindh governments instituted commissions to enforce the laws. The online survey found 70 per cent of the respondents knew a provincial protection law existed, but 65pc of them did not know where to find the commission’s office, obtain information, website or complaint route. Sixty-five per cent of the respondents reported experiencing work-related threats or interference since 2021. These findings describe the surveyed group rather than establishing province-wide prevalence. Challenges pinpointed The assessment identified distinct institutional challenges. Kamal Ud­­d­in Tipu, the federal commission’s cha­­irperson, spoke of staffing, budget, and administrative constraints during the research. With the federal commission now operational, the priority is to ensure that its personnel, resources and complaint systems support timely protection and sustained follow-up. In Sindh, the report documented an established institution with premises, meetings, complaints and engagement with police and media organisations. However, union representatives and non-official members described delayed responses, limited outreach beyond Karachi and dependence on police replies. The Sindh commission’s chairperson, Aijaz Ahmed Memon, disputed suggestions that journalists lacked trust in the institution and reported improvements in coordination, case activity and outreach plans. The report also highlighted media employers’ responsibilities. Fifty-one per cent of the respondents said employers had not informed them about safety procedures, emergency contacts, insurance, legal assistance or complaint mechanisms. The Sindh chairperson separately reported that 44 media outlets had not replied to the commission’s queries. Recommendations include confidential and accessible complaint routes, urgent risk assessment, designated caseworkers, police escalation procedures, stronger employer cooperation and publication of anonymised outcomes and spending. The report said amendments nee­ded to be framed carefully in order to address documented legal barriers. The Freedom Network called for coordinated action by governments, commissions, police, media employers and journalist organisations to deliver positive results and ensure that journalists can obtain effective assistance when threats arise. Published in Dawn, October 22nd, 2026
